info.name: Done n Dusted API (LD2)
info.description:
# Done n Dusted API (LD2)

A productivity system that plays like a tabletop RPG: a player logs real-life progress, the guild's game master approves it, and only approved log entries award XP.

Resource hierarchy: **Guild (1:N) → Quest (1:N) → LogEntry**. A child is reachable only through its parent, so a wrong chain returns `404`.

Access is controlled with **authentication and authorization**: JWT access and refresh tokens, the guild roles `PLAYER` / `DUNGEON_MASTER` and the global `ADMIN` role.

## How to run

1. Start the API (`./mvnw spring-boot:run`). It runs at `http://localhost:8080/api`.
2. In Postman, run the whole collection with **Run collection**. Keep the folders and requests in order: later requests use the IDs and tokens that earlier ones created.

Every run registers a new user, creates its own data and cleans up after itself, so the collection can be run any number of times.

## Authorization

The collection sets *Bearer Token* `{{accessToken}}`, which every request inherits. When another user sends a request, its *Authorization* tab names a different token:

| Token | User | Used for |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `accessToken` | `postman_<time>`, registered by the collection | Guild owner and game master |
| `playerToken` | `jonas` | Guild player (`PLAYER`) |
| `adminToken` | `admin` | Administrator (`ADMIN`) |

The demo users (`admin`, `rokas`, `ieva`, `jonas`) share the password `Demo123!`.

## Folders

| Folder | What it checks |
| --- | --- |
| 0. Authentication | Registration, login, JWT claims, `/auth/me`, token rotation, logout, `401` |
| 1. Overview | How many guilds, quests and log entries the database holds (with IDs), and whether child IDs point to the right parent |
| 2. Guilds | Guild CRUD, pagination via `links.next`, `400`, `404`, `409` and `415` errors |
| 3. Members | Adding members, roles, one game master per guild (`409`), `403`, `422` |
| 4. Quests | Creating quests, filters, XP calculation, `422` and the parent-chain `404` |
| 5. Log entries | A player logs progress, the game master approves it, XP rules, frozen content |
| 6. Roles and permissions | Who can do what: `403` for a non-member, a player, a game master with their own entry, a non-admin |
| 7. Cleanup | Deleting the created data (`204`, also by an administrator) and checking that it is gone |
| 8. Administration | User list, blocking and unblocking |

Every update is a `PATCH` (partial): only the fields sent change, so a description that is not sent is kept. A resource created without `description` stores it as `""`.

## Collection variables

| Variable | Value |
| --- | --- |
| `baseUrl` | API address, `http://localhost:8080/api` by default |
| `username`, `password`, `userId` | The user the collection registers; the demo users share the same password |
| `accessToken`, `refreshToken`, `oldRefreshToken` | The collection user's tokens and a used refresh token for the rotation test |
| `playerToken`, `playerId` | Token and ID of the player `jonas` |
| `adminToken`, `adminId` | Token and ID of the administrator |
| `guildName` | Unique guild name, generated by the create-guild request |
| `guildA`, `guildB` | IDs of the created guilds |
| `questId`, `logId` | IDs of the created quest and log entry |
| `logPlayer`, `logDm` | The player's and the game master's log entries for the permission checks |
| `occurredAt` | Event time (an hour ago) used for log entries |
| `nextPage`, `pageIds` | For the pagination demo: the `links.next` link and the first page's IDs |

## Error format

Every error comes back in the same `ApiError` shape:

```json
{
  "timestamp": "2026-09-21T09:15:30.123Z",
  "status": 403,
  "error": "Forbidden",
  "message": "You cannot review your own log entry.",
  "path": "/api/guilds/4/quests/10/logs/14",
  "details": [ { "field": "title", "message": "Must not be blank" } ]
}
```

`details` is included only when the error concerns specific fields.

**401 or 403?** `401`: the server does not know who you are (no token, a broken or expired token, wrong login details). `403`: it knows, but you lack the rights (not a guild member, the wrong guild role, not `ADMIN`, a blocked account).

**400 or 422?** `400` means the error is visible from the request alone (bad JSON, a wrong type, a field constraint, an unknown field). `422` means the request is well-formed but breaks a domain rule.

Every request has a saved example response (*Examples*) recorded from a real API run.

item.name: 0. Authentication
item.description:
Registration, login and the JWT token lifecycle.

* Every run registers a new user `postman_<time>`. This user creates the guilds, so it becomes their **owner and game master**.
* `accessToken` (a JWT valid for 15 min) is sent with every later request: collection *Authorization* → *Bearer Token* `{{accessToken}}`.
* `refreshToken` is single-use: once used at `/auth/refresh` it is revoked and a new pair is issued (rotation). A reused one is treated as stolen, and all of the user's sessions are revoked.
* At the end the collection logs in as the demo users `jonas` (player) and `admin` (administrator). Their password is `Demo123!`.

item.name: 1. Overview
item.description:
A database overview: how many guilds, quests and log entries there are, with all their IDs.

It runs as the administrator, because only an administrator sees everything. The folder can also run on its own (*Run folder*) at any time: it only reads and changes nothing.

item.name: Overview – guilds, quests and log entries

request.description:
Sums up all the data: how many guilds there are, how many quests they hold and how many log entries those quests have.

The response starts with `totalElements`, the total number of guilds, e.g. `{ "totalElements": 3, "content": [...] }`.

The test walks the whole **Guild → Quest → LogEntry** hierarchy: for each guild it fetches the quests, and for each quest its log entries. If a list does not fit on one page, it follows the `links.next` link the server returns.

The *Test Results* tab shows:

* a line per guild with its quest and log entry IDs;
* a total line, e.g. `Total - guilds: 3, quests: 9, log entries: 12` (a freshly seeded database).

It also checks that every quest's `guildId` and every log entry's `questId` point to a real parent and that no ID repeats.

The request is sent as the **administrator** (`adminToken`): only an administrator sees every guild and log entry. A pre-request script logs the administrator in, so the folder can also run on its own. The inner `pm.sendRequest` calls do not inherit the collection's authorization, so they add the `Authorization` header by hand.

exec: // The overview runs as ADMIN - only an administrator sees every guild and log entry.
// It logs in right here, so the folder can also run on its own.
body: { mode: 'raw', raw: JSON.stringify({ username: 'admin', password: pm.variables.get('password') }) }
const sortedIds = items => items.map(x => x.id).sort((a, b) => a - b).join(', ');
const get = url => new Promise((resolve, reject) =>
pm.sendRequest({ url, header: [{ key: 'Authorization', value: 'Bearer ' + pm.collectionVariables.get('adminToken') }] }, (err, res) => (err ? reject(err) : resolve(res.json()))));
// Collects every page of a list by following the server's links.next until there is none.
const guilds = (await getAll(pm.response.json())).sort((a, b) => a.id - b.id);
quests.forEach(q => { if (q.guildId !== guild.id) wrongParent.push(`quest ${q.id} points to guild ${q.guildId}`); });
logs.forEach(l => { if (l.questId !== quest.id) wrongParent.push(`log entry ${l.id} points to quest ${l.questId}`); });
pm.test(line, () => pm.expect(wrongParent, 'child objects point to the right parent ID').to.be.empty);
const summary = `Total - guilds: ${guilds.length}, quests: ${questIds.length}, log entries: ${logIds.length}`;
pm.expect(new Set(logIds).size, 'log entry IDs are unique').to.eql(logIds.length);
})().catch(err => pm.test('The overview ran without errors', () => { throw err; }));

item.name: 4. Quests
item.description:
Quests belong to a guild: `/guilds/{guildId}/quests`.

* `stat`: `STR`, `DEX`, `CON`, `INT`, `WIS`, `CHA`.
* `type`: `MILESTONE`, `HABIT`, `GRIND`, `SIDE_QUEST`. `targetCount` is required for the `GRIND` type and allowed only there.
* `difficulty` multiplies the base XP (10): `TRIVIAL` ×1, `EASY` ×2, `MEDIUM` ×3, `HARD` ×5, `LEGENDARY` ×8.

The server always calculates `xpPerCompletion`.

A guild member creates a quest (`createdBy`). The creator, the guild's game master or the owner can edit it; only the game master creates a `SIDE_QUEST` (see `6. Roles and permissions`).

request.description:

item.name: 5. Log entries
item.description:
Log entries belong to a quest: `/guilds/{guildId}/quests/{questId}/logs`.

* A new log entry is always created as `PENDING` with 0 XP. The server does not accept XP from the client on create.
* The game master approves (`APPROVED`) or rejects (`REJECTED`) a log entry with `PATCH`. Without `xpAwarded`, the server takes the XP from the quest's difficulty.
* `PENDING` and `REJECTED` log entries cannot have XP or inspiration.
* Approved XP is frozen: changing the quest's difficulty later does not rewrite history.
* The player `jonas` logs the entry and the guild's game master approves it. Nobody can approve their own log entry, not even the game master.

request.description:

A new log entry is always `PENDING`, with `xpAwarded = 0` and `inspirationAwarded = 0`. `occurredAt` cannot be in the future.

item.name: 6. Roles and permissions
item.description:
The authorization rules, each shown as a `403 Forbidden` response with an explanation.

| Who | Can |
| --- | --- |
| Guest | Only register and log in (`401` everywhere else) |
| `PLAYER` | See the guild and its quests, create quests, log and see **only their own** log entries |
| `DUNGEON_MASTER` | See every log entry in the guild, approve / reject them (not their own), create `SIDE_QUEST` |
| Owner | Edit and delete the guild, manage members |
| `ADMIN` | See every guild, delete any content, manage users |

A non-member gets nothing about a guild, only `403`.
